blocks.content: The Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.

items: Frequently Tested: The Oath of the Governor is administered by the Chief Justice of the High Court, NOT the President of India.
In the absence of the Chief Justice of India, the senior-most available judge of the Supreme Court administers the oath to the President.
The Governor is neither directly elected by the people nor indirectly elected by an electoral college; he is a central nominee.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The President of India takes an oath to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution, administered by the Chief Justice of India.
The Governor of a State is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
The Oath of office for the Governor is administered by the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court.
The Prime Minister is appointed by the President under Article 75, and other ministers are appointed on the advice of the Prime Minister.
Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts are appointed by the President after consultation with the judiciary.
